facts.text: Hartland Township is a civil township in eastern Livingston County, bordered on the east by Oakland County.
Hartland itself is an unincorporated community near the center of the township, just north of the junction of US 23 and M-59.
The township also includes the unincorporated community of Hallers Corners and part of Parshallville.
US 23 crosses the township as a four-lane freeway, with exits at M-59 and at Clyde Road.
The township's central business district is at the intersection of M-59 and US-23, where restaurants, retailers and professional services firms are concentrated.
Hartland's Village area is tucked into a historic residential area, with quaint buildings that house local businesses, the Music Hall and the Cromaine Library.
The Hartland Music Hall on Avon Street has been a center for musical performance and education in Hartland since the 1930s.
Hartland Township credits part of its growth to opportunities for rural, suburban and lake living.
Settlers Park, next to Township Hall on Clark Road, covers 100 acres of rolling fields, wooded areas and wetlands, with a paved bike path and a sledding hill.

christmas-light-installation.title: Christmas Light Installation in Hartland, MI
christmas-light-installation.meta_description: Hartland Township Christmas light installation for lake houses, rural acreage and subdivision homes, designed around how each is seen. Free estimates.
christmas-light-installation.h1: Christmas Light Installation in Hartland, MI
christmas-light-installation.hero_sub: From a lake house to a home on open acreage, we design the display for your property, hang it in clean lines and remove it once the holidays wrap up.
christmas-light-installation.local_paragraph: Hartland Township credits part of its growth to three kinds of living: rural, suburban and lake. Each one changes how a Christmas display should be planned. On a rural property the house may sit well back from the road, so the lighting has to read from a distance, and a lit tree line or wrapped evergreens by the drive can matter as much as the roofline. In a subdivision, a crisp roofline and tidy shrubs matter most, since the house is seen beside its neighbors. A lake home is seen from the water as well as the front, so the back of the house deserves attention too. We walk the property, design for how it is actually seen and handle installation, service and takedown.
considerations: When the house sits far from the road, fine detail gets lost. We favor strong roofline outlines, bold tree wraps and lit features near the drive, so the display reads clearly from the road and still looks polished when you pull up to the door.
The lake side of the house

Lake homes are often enjoyed most from the back and seen from across the water. We look at both faces of the house and can light the lakeside roofline, a bistro string over the deck or trees near the shore along with the front.

Long runs to a tree line or an entry at the end of a drive need a plan for power. We check outlet locations and distances during the estimate and design the runs so every section of the display has a sensible power source, even at the far end of the drive.
faq: Do you serve all of Hartland Township?

Hartland Township sits in eastern Livingston County, inside our service area. That includes the Hartland community near the center of the township as well as Hallers Corners and the township's share of Parshallville. Share your address using the form or by phone at (248) 756-8915, and we will confirm coverage and arrange an estimate.
Can you light trees far from the house?

Often, yes. Trees along a drive or a tree line at the edge of the yard can be lit when power can reach them sensibly. We look at distances, outlets and access during the estimate and explain what is practical before you decide on anything.

Earlier is better. The install window generally spans October into early December, and early requests get the widest choice of dates. Larger rural properties also take more time to plan, so starting in early fall gives the design room to come together without a rush.

commercial-holiday-lighting.title: Commercial Holiday Lighting in Hartland, MI
commercial-holiday-lighting.meta_description: Hartland Township commercial holiday lighting for businesses at M-59 and US-23, the Village area, offices and HOAs. Design, install and takedown.
commercial-holiday-lighting.h1: Commercial Holiday Lighting in Hartland, MI
commercial-holiday-lighting.hero_sub: Restaurants, retailers, professional offices and association entrances lit for the season, planned for traffic on M-59 and neighbors in the Village area.
commercial-holiday-lighting.local_paragraph: Hartland's commercial life is split between two very different settings. The central business district sits at the intersection of M-59 and US-23, where restaurants, retailers and professional services firms are concentrated around the freeway exit. There, holiday lighting has to read at a glance: bold building outlines, wrapped trees at the entry and lit walkways that stand out from the road. The Village area is tucked into a historic residential neighborhood, where quaint buildings house local businesses, the Music Hall and the Cromaine Library, and it suits warmer, more detailed lighting. Across the township, subdivision and condo entrances can get the same seasonal attention.
considerations: Near the M-59 and US-23 interchange, people often see your property first through a windshield. Simple, strong outlines on the roofline and facade, plus wrapped trees near the entrance, read better at driving speed than scattered accents. We design for that view first, then refine the details for people on foot.

The Village area's quaint buildings have a scale and charm that heavy lighting would overwhelm. Warm white outlines, a framed window or a pair of wrapped trees by the door can frame the entrance without competing with the architecture around them.

Where a Hartland subdivision has an entrance sign or monument, lighting it together with the trees and plantings around it makes the whole neighborhood feel cared for in winter. A single estimate for the association carries the job from design to takedown.
faq: Which Hartland Township businesses can you light?

Restaurants, retailers, professional offices and other businesses in Hartland Township are within our service area, from the M-59 and US-23 business district to the Village area. Reach out through the form or at (248) 756-8915, and we will take it from there.
Can you light a subdivision entrance for our HOA?

Yes. HOA and subdivision entrances are part of our commercial work. We can walk the entrance with a board member, plan the look and put every piece of the job in a written estimate, a simple document to bring to the full board for a vote.
How far ahead should a business plan?

Plan in early fall if you can. Landlords and associations often want to see a written plan before they approve exterior work, and commercial displays go up from October into early December. Starting early leaves room for both the sign-off and the install date you prefer.

permanent-lighting.title: Permanent Christmas Lights in Hartland, MI
permanent-lighting.meta_description: Hartland permanent Christmas lights for lake houses, rural properties and subdivision homes, with app-controlled colors and schedules. Free estimates.
permanent-lighting.hero_sub: One installation, then a roofline you can light for any occasion from your phone. Holidays, game days, lake evenings and everyday accent light.
permanent-lighting.local_paragraph: In a township known for rural, suburban and lake living, permanent lighting can do a different job on every kind of property. Mounted along the roofline a single time, the lights stay up all year and take their cues from an app on your phone. Warm white carries the Christmas season. Team colors come out on game day. On a lake home, a soft outline can make the house look finished from the water on a summer night. On a rural property with a long drive, a scheduled glow makes the house easy to find after dark. From there, we handle the layout, power and runs, install everything and teach you the app.
considerations: A long main roof, an attached garage and an outbuilding can all be part of the plan, or not. We decide together which rooflines to light, so the outline looks intentional and the investment goes where it shows from the road and the yard.

On a lake home, the side facing the water may deserve light as much as the street side. We look at both during the estimate and route the runs so the outline reads cleanly from the lake as well as from the drive.

A schedule can bring a warm outline on at dusk and switch it off at bedtime, with colors saved for holidays, birthdays and game days. We set up the first schedules with you at the end of the install, and after that the lights run on their own.
faq: Does your permanent lighting service reach all of Hartland Township?

Yes. Homes throughout Hartland Township are within our service area, including rural and lake properties. The free estimate means a walk around your roofline and power sources, a talk about how you plan to use the lights and a written plan of what is included.
Does it work on lake homes?

Generally, yes. Lake homes often have long rooflines, porches and more than one face to consider. We plan the layout during the estimate, including the lake side if you want it lit, and point out where the lights will shine and where they will not.
Will I still need seasonal lights for trees?

Permanent lighting covers the roofline. If you also want trees, shrubs or a drive lit for the holidays, we can add seasonal lighting to those areas, installed in the fall and taken down after the holidays. Your estimate can include both.
